slides.title: SAT math question of the week

blocks.text: What is the value of x + y?

items: From the second equation, x = y + 1.
Put that into the first: 2(y + 1) + 3y = 12, so 5y = 10 and y = 2.
The question asks for x + y = 3 + 2.

caption:
The most common algebra slip on the SAT is not hard maths. It is a minus sign in front of a bracket.

The minus applies to everything inside. Write the extra line, every time.

slides.title: The minus sign that costs the most points

blocks.text: Simplify this. Most wrong answers come from one step.
The minus was applied to 2x but not to the −3. Inside the bracket, −3 becomes +3.

items: The minus sign multiplies everything in the bracket: −(2x − 3) = −2x + 3.
